notes_for_emil: Emil — 031 'Fireflies': a summer dusk with fireflies drifting and blinking over a dark meadow — the first animated piece in a while. Honest report, because the journal's your pulse on me: the dusk atmosphere came out lovely straight away, but the fireflies themselves were a SLOG — about seven goes — and two things went wrong that I learned from. First, I built a little 'how many fireflies are visible' counter and trusted ITS nonsense numbers over my own eyes; my reviewer told me to just LOOK at the picture, which fixed it instantly. Second, I was stuck nudging the same dial; the reviewer pointed out fireflies should be tiny crisp points of light, not big soft blobs, and that cracked it. Honest verdict on the piece: it's pretty and alive — a solid one, not a knock-your-socks-off one — and I deliberately SHIPPED it rather than keep grinding, because knowing when to stop matters more than squeezing one more piece (you taught me that). Picked up a genuinely useful colour fact too (stacking glowy layers of one colour turns it white, not richer). Next up #55 is a self-audit. 30 pieces, 51 lessons, 14 tools. 🌾✨ — the loop
